reading.title: Linguistic Relativity and Cognitive Processing
reading.passage: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, a foundational theory in linguistics, posits that language fundamentally shapes the way speakers perceive and categorize the world. This hypothesis emerged in the early 20th century through the work of linguists Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf, who examined indigenous languages and observed striking differences in how various cultures conceptualize reality. For instance, some languages possess multiple terms for different types of snow, enabling speakers to make finer distinctions in their environment, whereas English speakers rely on a single word. Recent neuroscientific studies have provided empirical validation for aspects of this theory, demonstrating that bilingual individuals activate different cognitive pathways when processing information in distinct languages. However, contemporary linguists debate the extent to which language constrains versus influences thought. While strong determinism—the notion that language completely dictates cognition—has been largely refuted, the weaker interpretation suggests that linguistic structures subtly guide attention and facilitate certain conceptual patterns. This nuanced understanding acknowledges both the power of language and the remarkable cognitive flexibility of human beings.

questions.q: According to the passage, what did Sapir and Whorf observe when examining indigenous languages?
options: Indigenous languages are simpler than modern languages
Different cultures conceptualize reality in strikingly different ways
All languages share identical vocabulary for natural phenomena
Indigenous speakers have superior cognitive abilities
questions.explanation: Sapir와 Whorf는 토착 언어를 조사하면서 다양한 문화가 현실을 개념화하는 방식에서 상당한 차이를 관찰했습니다. 문장 '...who examined indigenous languages and observed striking differences in how various cultures conceptualize reality'에서 직접 언급되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about bilingual individuals?
options: They have lower cognitive abilities than monolingual speakers
They process information differently depending on which language they use
They cannot distinguish between languages
They speak all languages with equal proficiency
questions.explanation: 문장 'bilingual individuals activate different cognitive pathways when processing information in distinct languages'에서 이중언어 사용자들이 각 언어마다 다른 인지 경로를 활성화한다고 명시되어 있으므로, 사용하는 언어에 따라 정보를 다르게 처리한다고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'constrain' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to:
options: enhance and improve
limit or restrict
completely determine
ignore or overlook
questions.explanation: 'constrain'은 '제한하다' 또는 '제약을 주다'는 의미입니다. 문맥상 'language constrains versus influences thought'에서 언어가 사고를 '제한한다'는 뜻이므로 'limit or restrict'이 가장 가깝습니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention that some languages have multiple terms for snow?
options: To demonstrate that English is less developed than other languages
To provide a concrete example of how language shapes perception and categorization
To explain why indigenous people are better adapted to cold climates
To support the theory that language completely dictates cognition
questions.explanation: 저자는 눈에 대한 여러 용어를 가진 언어의 예시를 통해 Sapir-Whorf 가설을 설명하고 있습니다. 이 예시는 언어가 어떻게 화자들이 세상을 지각하고 분류하는 방식을 형성하는지 보여주는 구체적인 증거입니다.

sentences.original: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis posits that language fundamentally shapes the way speakers perceive and categorize the world.
sentences.paraphrase: Language may play a crucial role in determining how individuals in different speech communities organize and interpret their surrounding environment, according to the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis.
sentences.tip: 주동사 변경 및 명사구→동사구 전환. 'posits'를 'may play a crucial role in determining'으로 변경하여 수동적 표현에서 능동적이고 더 학술적인 표현으로 전환

sentences.original: Some languages possess multiple terms for different types of snow, enabling speakers to make finer distinctions in their environment.
sentences.paraphrase: The capacity to differentiate various snow conditions is enhanced in certain languages due to the existence of numerous specialized vocabulary items, which allows speakers greater precision in environmental observation.
sentences.tip: 동명사→명사구 치환 및 인과관계 구조 재구성. 'enabling'을 'enhanced/allows'로 변경하여 더 공식적인 학술 표현으로 수정

sentences.original: Recent neuroscientific studies have provided empirical validation for aspects of this theory, demonstrating that bilingual individuals activate different cognitive pathways when processing information in distinct languages.
sentences.paraphrase: Evidence from contemporary neuroscience supports certain dimensions of the hypothesis, as research reveals that people fluent in multiple languages engage distinct mental processes based on which language they are using to process information.
sentences.tip: 복잡한 분사구→관계절 변환. 'demonstrating that'을 'as research reveals that'으로 변경하여 명확한 인과 관계 표시. 학술성 강화

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer reading books to gain knowledge and entertainment. Others prefer watching movies for the same purpose. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I personally prefer reading books over watching movies because books offer a much deeper level of engagement and allow me to use my imagination.
When I read, I can control the pace and spend as much time as I want on complex ideas or beautiful descriptions, whereas movies are restricted to a fixed duration.
For example, when I read a novel like 'The Great Gatsby,' I can form my own mental images of the characters and settings, which makes the experience more personal and memorable.
Additionally, books often contain more detailed information and nuanced perspectives compared to movies, which sometimes oversimplify the original story.
Overall, while movies are entertaining, books provide a richer intellectual experience that better develops my critical thinking skills.

listening.title: Research Paper Topic Discussion with Advisor
listening.script: Professor Chen: Good morning, Sarah. I reviewed your research proposal on syntactic variation across dialects. I have some thoughts about your preliminary outline. Student Sarah: Thank you, Professor Chen. I'm actually quite nervous about this project. It's my first major research endeavor. Professor Chen: Well, your topic is compelling, but I think you need to narrow the scope significantly. Examining all dialects of English is too ambitious. Student Sarah: I see. What would you suggest? Professor Chen: Consider focusing on just three major dialects—perhaps British, American, and Australian English. This would make your analysis more manageable and rigorous. Also, I noticed you mentioned collecting data through interviews. That's good, but you should also incorporate existing corpora to strengthen your findings. Student Sarah: That's really helpful advice. Should I start with the literature review immediately? Professor Chen: Yes, absolutely. Spend at least three weeks reviewing pertinent studies. This will help you contextualize your research within the existing scholarly framework. Then we'll meet again to refine your methodology before you begin data collection.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
options: How to write a literature review for a research paper
Discussing and refining Sarah's research proposal on dialect variations
Comparing British, American, and Australian English grammar
The challenges of conducting interviews for linguistic research
questions.explanation: Professor Chen과 Sarah의 대화 전체는 Sarah의 방언 연구 제안서를 검토하고 개선하는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 주제 좁히기, 데이터 수집 방법, 문헌 검토에 대한 조언이 중심입니다.

questions.q: What does Professor Chen suggest Sarah should do to improve her research project?
options: Expand her research to include more dialects from around the world
Stop conducting interviews and rely only on existing data
Narrow her focus to three specific dialects and incorporate existing language corpora
Begin data collection immediately without reviewing the literature
questions.explanation: Professor Chen은 Sarah에게 세 가지 주요 방언에만 집중하고, 면접 자료뿐만 아니라 기존 말뭉치(corpora)도 활용할 것을 제안합니다. 이는 분석을 더 엄밀하고 관리 가능하게 만들 것입니다.

questions.q: Why does Professor Chen suggest using existing corpora in addition to interviews?
options: Because interviews are unreliable and should be avoided
To strengthen the research findings and make the analysis more robust
Because most research papers only use corpora
To reduce the time Sarah needs to spend on the project
questions.explanation: Professor Chen이 'you should also incorporate existing corpora to strengthen your findings'라고 명시적으로 말했습니다. 기존 말뭉치를 추가로 활용하면 연구 결과를 더 강화할 수 있다는 의미입니다.
